newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end mixed, funds hit soyoil late.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end mixed, funds hit soyoil late.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures ended mixed Monday, with soyoil futures tumbling late on heavy commodity fund selling, CBOT floor traders said.
In late trading, Rosenthal Collins sold 800 lots March and Griffin Trading sold 300 lots March.
Weakness in soybean futures was also cited as a reason that both product markets lost strength in late trading.
Soymeal ended mostly higher but near session lows. Soymeal had rallied on demand-related strength for most of the session.
Very cold weather in the U.S. Midwest, U.S. Plains and Europe was seen causing an increase in demand for feed, traders said.
There were also reports from cash sources Monday of meal sales to Europe. The business was said to be linked to greater demand from feed companies linked to cold weather there.
CBOT soymeal ended down $0.20 to up $1.00 per ton, with January up $0.90 at $228.70 and March up $0.40 at $221.30 a ton.
Soyoil futures settled down 0.04 to 0.12 cent per lb with January down 0.06 at 22.95 cents and March down 0.09 at 23.30.
In options trading, Cargill bought 500 July $2.20 per ton soymeal calls and 110 March $2.40 calls, pit sources said.
In other late trade, Produce Grain bought 250 lots March and soyoil Prudential Securities and Smith Barney each bought 200 March.
On the day, Term Commodities bought 600 lots May soyoil. Refco bought 1,400 lots March soymeal.

Soyoil futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 20,000 contracts, below the 20,450 traded Friday. Soymeal futures volume was estimated at 22,000 contracts, above the 18,505 traded Friday, the exchange said.
